text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Oposition parties quarrel over beer excise and the right-wing Fatherland Union is accused of supporting its sponsors as it wants a lower excise duty for locally-made beer.

- Russian experts have agreed not to demand a joint group to investigate the situation of Russians in Estonia as a foreign ministers' agreement initially required. The Estonian foreign ministry also quotes them as saying that they have revised some of their views on human rights in Estonia.
- The parliament debates a law on protection of small islands but the government opposes the draft.
- The wages of public prosecutors will rise significantly from January 1 in order to prevent them from leaving their jobs for privately-owned law offices.
- Estonian and Russian foreign ministers are not to meet in Brussels today during the NACC meeting.
- Russia is still demanding that Estonia grant citizenship to all residents who want it. Most Russians in Estonia are not citizens of the country.
- The British House of Lords approved the Estonian association agreement with the EU. The House of Commons is to debate it next week.
- Estonia will open its new office at the European Union in Brussels today.
- Estonia and Kenya will conclude diplomatic relations, five more African nations are to follow.
- Estonian computer hackers are accused of having destroyed data in a Taiwanese computer and the firm has demanded compensation.
- The Tallinn heating firm intends to reduce the price of heating for firms and to raise it for individual customers.
- A Finnish shipping firm is likely to begin operating passanger ferry 'Vana Tallinn' between Estonia and Finland.
